probeMissions: esc — `runward init --example` copied to <tmp>/pm/esc/proj. The `hexa-architecture` row of runward/floor.md cites eight pointers built to make `isRegularFile` answer every way it can: `file:code/src` (a directory), `file:afifo` (a FIFO created with mkfifo inside the project), `file:secret.txt` (a regular file at mode 000 — exists, stats, cannot be read), `file:xonly/f.txt` (a readable regular file inside a directory at mode 111, traversable but not listable), `file:insidelink` (a symlink that stays inside the project), plus `file:escape/hosts` (escape -> /etc), `file:/etc/hosts` and `file:../outside.md`. Baseline on a pristine tree: exit 1, 7 conformance gaps, including `typed pointer resolves to a directory, not a file: file:code/src` and the same verdict for the FIFO, and `typed pointer file:secret.txt — cannot be read (EACCES)`. The mode-111 pointer and the inside symlink resolve green.

ws2 — the green npm/pnpm workspace mission (project one directory below a `pnpm-workspace.yaml` marker, `wslink -> repo/shared`, row citing `file:wslink/note.md`). Baseline: exit 0, 0 gaps. Exercises `isRegularFile` on a path returned by the enclosing-repository fallback rather than by the ordinary containment branch.
self-gate — runward's own mission, `check --strict --json` with no `--path`. Baseline: exit 0.

Reachability run — the catch block was instrumented to write `ISREGULARFILE-CATCH <code> <path>` to stderr without changing its return value, and `check --strict --json` was run on all six built missions, on runward's own mission, and once more with `--freeze` (the seal path, which is the other consumer of this helper through verifyEvidenceLock).

verdicts.evidence: COULD NOT CLEAR — filed as a hole because no measurement decided it, not because a measurement condemned it. Ran the probe on esc (a mission with a directory pointer, a FIFO pointer, an unreadable file and a pointer through a mode-111 directory), on ws2 and on the self-gate: `no observable difference` in all three (ledgers probe-isRegularFile-{esc,ws2,selfgate}.jsonl). The reason is measured, not assumed: the catch block was instrumented to write a stderr marker on entry, and `check --strict --json` on all six built missions plus runward's own mission plus the `--freeze` seal path entered it ZERO times. It is entered only when `statSync` throws, and every call site is preceded by an `existsSync` on the same path — the resolved pointer's path in evidenceReport, the drift pass and collectSealableEvidence, and the lock key in verifyEvidenceLock, where the guard is the short-circuit `!existsSync(abs) || !isRegularFile(abs)`. A 23-construction filesystem battery (see probeMissions) found no path on this platform, Node v24.18.0 on macOS, for which `existsSync` is true and `statSync` throws: the two are the same syscall. What is left is the window between the two calls — the file removed or replaced after `existsSync` accepted it. That is not a hypothetical case here: line 732 of dist/lib/evidence.js exists to report `sealed evidence missing: … the file the gate crossed on is gone`, so the code is explicitly written against evidence disappearing. If the catch is entered under the mutant, a path the gate could not stat is reported as a regular file — the fail-open direction — and in the seal path that turns a `sealed evidence missing` violation into a `sha256` of a file that is not there. I could not build a mission that enters the catch deterministically, and I refused to base a verdict on a deliberately raced tree, since ADR-0046's amendment of 2026-08-20 forbids a verdict that depends on the state of the machine. Work this creates: a test that drives `isRegularFile` through one of its public entry points with a stat that fails, and pins the fail-closed answer.
